title: Fit a spring tension rod between two cupboard walls so it holds itself up, level and at a marked height
instruction: Fit the spring tension rod between the two white cupboard walls, level, at the yellow band.
context: Spring tension rods are a familiar household fitting: people put them up in a cupboard, alcove or window recess to hang a curtain, clothes or spray bottles, or to divide a shelf, because they need no drilling. Many people have had one fall as soon as it was let go, or slip down crooked a day later. Unlike TK-8WZPBE (squeeze a cage fastener's legs; hooks retain it), nothing holds this rod up but its own spring and the grip of its rubber tips.
setup: 'In front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, the midline is halfway between the arm bases. Cupboard walls (fixed, white painted board): two boards standing on the table, each 170 mm front to back (25.0 to 42.0 cm in front of the bases), 20 mm thick and 200 mm tall, their inner faces 150 mm left and 150 mm right of the midline (a 300 mm gap). Yellow band: a strip 20 mm wide, 30 mm tall and 2 mm proud on each wall's front edge (the face toward the robot), from 120 to 150 mm above the table. Spring tension rod (loose, 100 g in all) with the diameter of an off-the-shelf 7/16 in round spring tension rod (for example Graber's 7/16 in round spring tension rod for 11 to 18 in openings), set to 325 mm, within that range and 25 mm (about 1 in) longer than the gap, as spring rods are fitted: a blue outer tube 11.1 mm (7/16 in) across and 180 mm long with a black rubber tip 19 mm across and 10 mm proud of its end (60 g together), and a grey inner tube 10.3 mm (13/32 in) across and 170 mm long with an identical tip (40 g). The inner tube slides in the outer one, guided by the outer tube's bore over at least 45 mm of overlap, against a 200 N/m coil spring inside the outer tube; a pin across the inner tube running in two 51.5 mm slots in the outer tube (50 mm of travel) keeps them together. A red line painted round the inner tube 5 mm out from the outer tube's mouth at full length disappears into the mouth once the rod is squeezed 5 mm. Free length, tip face to tip face, 325 mm; it can be squeezed by up to 50 mm. README.md gives a build to these sizes (tubes, spring, attachment, guide and ballast). The colours are for the simulator's camera view; the retail rod is white. The rod lies left to right, outer tube on the left, its middle 17.0 cm in front of the bases on the midline and its axis 35.6 mm above the table, on two risers, grey plastic blocks 40 mm front to back, 20 mm wide and 30 mm tall taped to the table, 3 cm left and 6 cm right of the midline. Friction, static / sliding: rod and tips 1.0 / 0.8, walls 0.6 / 0.5. Spring damping 1 N s/m. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged after the robot's last release. No part of the robot may touch the rod or come within 5 mm of it after that, and the 10 s hold must finish within the 40 s run limit. The rod holds itself up when each tip touches its wall's inner face (a sheet of office paper slid down the wall face is stopped by the tip) with its centre on the wall (between the front and back edges, not above the top), the rod is squeezed at least 5 mm (the red line on the inner tube is hidden in the outer tube), it is at least 3 mm clear of the table, and it stays put hands-off for 10 s: no visible movement for 5 s, then a 300 g weight hung gently at its middle for the last 5 s moves neither tip more than 2 mm from pencil marks made when it goes on. A tilted or skewed rod counts if it passes. Score 1.0: it holds itself up, each tip wholly on its wall (centre at least 9.5 mm inside the front and back edges, top not above the wall top), both tip centres 120 to 150 mm above the table (in the yellow band), within 10 mm of the same height and within 10 mm of each other front to back (a ruler). Score 0.5: it holds itself up but misses any of those placement limits. Score 0: anything else: on the table, risers or wall tops, in front of or behind the walls, a tip off its wall, still touched, sliding, falling or slipping under the weight. The trial ends at 1.0 once the 1.0 condition holds for 1 s after the 10 s hold; otherwise the last step is scored.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Between trials: 1. Squeeze the rod and take it out from between the walls. 2. Let it spring back to its full 325 mm (check it with a tape). 3. Check the two 30 mm risers are taped 17 cm in front of the arm bases, 3 cm left and 6 cm right of the midline. 4. Lay the rod on them left to right, outer tube on the left, its middle on the midline. 5. Check the walls have not moved (inner faces 150 mm either side of the midline).
fidelity: Approximate. Tubes and tips are rigid cylinders, walls two fixed boards. The rod has the diameter of the Graber 7/16 in rod and is set to 325 mm, within its 11 to 18 in range. Its spring rate is not published and is likely stiffer; the model's linear 200 N/m is what the two arms can squeeze far enough to clear the gap. Fitted, squeezed 25 mm, each tip presses with 5 N, holding the rod and the 300 g test weight about twice over.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the rod stays on its risers). Scripted demo: 1.0 (the rod holds itself level in the band, hands-off for 10 s including the 300 g test load, after both grippers withdraw).
